stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $0.6$ in this context?
stimulus: During a drought, a hydrologist models the depth of water in a reservoir with the equation $D = 42 - 0.6t$, where $D$ is the depth of the water, in meters, $t$ days after the drought began.
choices: The depth of the water when the drought began, in meters
The decrease in the depth of the water each day, in meters
The increase in the depth of the water each day, in meters
The number of days it takes the depth to drop by 1 meter
explanation: The model has the form $D = b + mt$, with slope $m = -0.6$. The slope is a rate: each day $t$ goes up by 1, so $D$ changes by $-0.6$ meters. The sign tells you the depth goes down, so $0.6$ is the number of meters the water depth drops each day.

A.why: You gave the meaning of the constant term. The depth when the drought began is the value at $t = 0$, which is $42$, not $0.6$. You described the intercept when the question asked about the slope.

C.why: You read the size of the rate but dropped the minus sign in front of it. Because the term is $-0.6t$, the depth falls as time passes. It does not rise.

D.why: You flipped the rate. $0.6$ is meters per day, not days per meter. A drop of 1 meter would take $\frac{1}{0.6}$ days, which is a different quantity.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line in this context?
stimulus: A county health clinic stocked flu vaccine doses before a vaccination drive and received no new shipments during the drive. The graph shows the number of doses remaining in stock, $y$, $x$ days after the drive began.

figure.caption: Flu Vaccine Doses Remaining
figure.alt: A straight line graph of doses remaining against days after the drive began, falling from the vertical axis to the horizontal axis.

choices: The clinic gives out 80 doses each day.
The clinic gives out 480 doses each day.
The clinic gives out 40 doses each day.
The clinic receives 40 doses each day.
explanation: Pick two clear grid points, such as $(0, 480)$ and $(2, 400)$. The slope is $\frac{400 - 480}{2 - 0} = -40$. The stock goes down by 40 doses per day, and since no shipments arrive, that drop is the number of doses given out. The clinic gives out 40 doses each day.

A.why: You found the 80-dose drop between two gridlines, but that drop happens over 2 days. You never divided by the run of 2 to get a per-day rate.

B.why: 480 is where the line meets the vertical axis. That is the starting stock, which is the y-intercept. It is not the slope.

D.why: You got the size of the slope right but not its direction. The line falls, so the slope is negative and the stock goes down. The clinic is not receiving doses.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $150$ in this context?
stimulus: After rats were removed from a small island in 2015, ecologists modeled the number of seabird nesting pairs on the island with the function $P(x) = 150 + 35x$, where $P(x)$ is the estimated number of nesting pairs $x$ years after 2015.
choices: The estimated increase in nesting pairs each year
The estimated number of nesting pairs in 2016
The estimated greatest number of pairs the island can hold
The estimated number of nesting pairs in 2015
explanation: $150$ is the constant term, so it is the value of $P(x)$ when $x = 0$. Here $x$ counts years after 2015, so $x = 0$ means 2015 itself. The model estimates 150 nesting pairs in 2015.

A.why: You described the slope. The yearly increase is the coefficient of $x$, which is $35$. It is not the constant $150$.

B.why: You treated 2016 as the starting year. Since $x$ is the number of years after 2015, $x = 0$ is 2015. The 2016 estimate is $P(1) = 185$.

C.why: A linear model keeps growing and has no upper limit, so nothing in it describes the island's capacity. $150$ is where the model starts, not a ceiling.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $4$ in this context?
stimulus: A field linguist estimates the time needed to transcribe recorded interviews in an endangered language with the equation $T = 4r + 30$, where $T$ is the total number of minutes of work and $r$ is the number of minutes of recorded audio.
choices: Each additional minute of audio adds 4 minutes of work.
Each additional 4 minutes of audio adds 1 minute of work.
The linguist spends 4 minutes on setup before any audio.
Each additional minute of audio adds 34 minutes of work.
explanation: $4$ is the coefficient of $r$, so it is the rate of change of $T$ with respect to $r$. Each time $r$ goes up by 1 minute of audio, $T$ goes up by 4 minutes of work.

B.why: You flipped the rate. The slope is minutes of work per minute of audio. You divided output by input the wrong way around and got minutes of audio per minute of work.

C.why: You gave the coefficient the job of the constant. The fixed work done before any audio is the value at $r = 0$, which is $30$ minutes.

D.why: $34$ is $T$ when $r = 1$, which is the total work for a 1-minute recording, setup included. Each additional minute adds only the slope, $4$ minutes. The 30-minute setup is not repeated.

stem: Which of the following is the best interpretation of $2{,}500$ in this context?
stimulus: At an excavation site, archaeologists estimate the age of material in a sediment layer with the equation $A = 2{,}500d + 400$, where $A$ is the estimated age of the material, in years, and $d$ is the depth of the layer below the surface, in meters.
choices: Material at the surface is estimated to be 2,500 years old.
Each additional meter of depth adds 2,500 years of age.
Each additional centimeter of depth adds 2,500 years of age.
Each additional meter of depth removes 2,500 years of age.
explanation: $2{,}500$ is the coefficient of $d$, so it is the slope. It is measured in years per meter. The coefficient is positive, so every additional meter of depth raises the estimated age by 2,500 years.

A.why: The surface is depth $d = 0$, and there the age is the constant term, $400$ years. You gave the slope the meaning of the intercept.

C.why: You used the wrong unit for $d$. Depth is measured in meters, so the rate is 2,500 years per meter. One centimeter would add only 25 years.

D.why: The coefficient is positive, so age goes up as depth goes up: deeper layers are older. You reversed the direction of the relationship.
